chapters.title: A parity check becomes a circuit
Load beliefs into the fixed graph
Vanilla BP: repeat until the checks agree
Relay BP: retain memory, restart messages

captions.text: A column is a variable. A row is a parity check.
Each 1 in H becomes one connection between its variable and check.
One edge keeps the same identity in the matrix, Scala port map, and circuit.
Scala builds the hardware before decoding. All these units exist together.
These integer priors are teaching inputs. Their positive signs favor no error.
Load stores the syndrome and priors, then initializes every variable-to-check register.
Positive belief: no error. Negative belief: error. Magnitude measures confidence.
The CNU finds the smallest two magnitudes, preserving equal minima.
For v3, remove v3's contribution. Syndrome 1 makes the outgoing sign negative.
Hardware sends a shared min-pair plus sign and useSecond bits to each neighbor.
All CNUs compute in parallel. Their results latch on the first iteration clock.
The full signed total determines the decision before marginal saturation.
An extrinsic message excludes the recipient's evidence, so it is not the marginal.
The same rule works at a higher-degree variable. Each neighbor gets its own message.
All VNUs commit together on the second clock. One complete BP iteration is finished.
We now load uniform priors, so this frame needs more than one iteration.
Residual 100: the first check still disagrees. Continue.
Residual 000: stop after two iterations, four clocks after accepted load.
Output stays valid until accepted. A syndrome match alone does not establish logical success.
Relay changes the VNU bias using the previous marginal at every iteration.
Leg 0 starts with β = 7/8. Later legs draw deterministic per-variable coefficients.
Within leg 0, β stays fixed while the marginal and next iteration's bias change.
Leg 0 matches the syndrome. The target is two candidates, so a new leg begins.
Keep the new marginals; restart edge messages and the local schedule. No extra clock.
Leg 1 finds the same correction. Repeated candidates count toward the target.
Three iterations cost six core clocks. The equal-score tie keeps the earlier correction.
Same graph, same message-passing phases. Relay adds memory and leg scheduling.
